problem: Commercial search demand can be diluted when a new page is created for an intent already owned by an existing money page.
root_cause: SEO opportunity detection can overvalue keyword volume without first binding the query to an existing canonical intent owner and downstream conversion path.
prevention: Prefer the existing canonical money page when the search intent is already owned.
Create a new landing page or blog only when SERP evidence proves a distinct intent gap.
Route commercial money pages toward the canonical Frisse blik conversion step and preserve a secondary direct-contact route.
Treat singular/plural query variants as one intent owner unless evidence proves otherwise.
Measure SEO success through qualified traffic, Frisse blik starts, leads, orders and attributable revenue.
expected_outcome: Higher commercial relevance and clearer conversion routing without adding cannibalising pages.

historical_replay: Existing canonical owners retained for Exact Online, generic API-koppeling and Twinfield queries
No competing landing page or blog created for plural Twinfield variant
evaluation.expected: Each validated commercial query resolves to one canonical money-page owner with a measurable Frisse-blik conversion path and no new cannibalising page.
invariants: one canonical money-page owner per commercial intent cluster
new page only when SERP evidence proves a distinct intent gap
commercial SEO page exposes a direct conversion path to Frisse blik and/or contact
SEO success is measured downstream through qualified leads, orders and attributable revenue
